text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open lower on Monday, with investors taking their cue from a softer bond market and fearful of a resumption of selling in the high technology sector.
"We had a sloppy day Friday, particularly where the techs were concerned, and I think the opening will reflect that," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.

He said the start of a Robertson Stephens Tech '97 Investors Conference in San Francisco could spark some strength among the high technology issues. The Dow Jones industrial average rose 4.42 points on Friday to close at 6,931.62, down 57.34 points on the week.
